The model represents spectral bands as trapezoidal shapes defined by their position and width.
*   $I(s + \Delta s, \lambda)$ is the intensity at the next integration step.
*   $\rho_m(s)$ is the scalar density of material $m$ at position $s$.
*   $E_m(\lambda)$ is the emitted power of material $m$ at wavelength $\lambda$.
*   $A_m(\lambda)$ is the absorption coefficient of material $m$ at wavelength $\lambda$.
*   $\Delta s$ is the step size along the ray.
A discrete spectral representation method where the spectrum is divided into N uniform bands by point-sampling at uniform intervals.

It is used to approximate spectral distribution functions for volume rendering but suffers from energy conservation loss, information loss during Doppler shifts, and accuracy issues. [Link](3468-point-sampled-spectrum-model.md)
